chunks: From him, from his father, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:
I asked him about a man who dies and has no household goods; he said: 'The sword, the weapons, the saddle, and the clothes of his skin.'

key_terms.ثِيَابُ جِلْدِهِ: Clothes of his skin / his clothing

ai.seo_question: What personal items does a deceased man retain according to Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between general household wealth and personal effects, specifically identifying the sword, weapons, saddle, and clothing as the exclusive property of the deceased man. This ruling reflects the pre-Islamic and early Islamic context where martial equipment and personal attire were distinct from communal or familial assets, a principle later integrated into Shia inheritance jurisprudence to ensure equitable distribution among heirs.
